events.price_note: $12 general; $10 for members, Gray Area members, and students
events.title: CROSSROADS 2026 — Program 3: we name no heroes
events.why: Today’s most immediate experimental-film detour: a 63-minute program treats damaged prints, colonial histories, and archive debris as raw material rather than museum matter.

events.title: Push Buttons and AI
events.why: An unusually specific counterspell to empty AI boosterism: films and a live discussion on automation, chatbot intimacy, hidden annotation labor, machine vision, and model collapse.

events.title: Agentworld x Superdark Factory
events.why: Closest thing to a Deliria2 afterimage this week: Bratton and Poliks make hybrid human-AI society and automated agentic systems philosophically strange rather than pitch-deck bland.

events.title: Artist Shaghayegh Cyrous with Abby Chen
events.why: A compact art-tech chamber piece: a mythopoetic multimedia installation about migration and power, followed by an artist-curator conversation instead of a white-cube checkbox.

events.title: Tank Houses in Northwest Berkeley
events.why: A three-mile piece of stubbornly local infrastructure archaeology: trace six surviving windmill-topped water towers and how pre-EBMUD Berkeley pressurized domestic water.

events.title: Stanford LASER: Real and Artificial Minds, AI for Artists, Satirical Art
events.why: An actual art-science salon, not startup-scented AI group therapy: a cognitive scientist, neuroscientist, and visual artist triangulate minds, machine culture, and critical wit.

events.title: Algorithmic Art Assembly presents: Kit Clayton
events.why: The credible old-Bay-New-Media nerve: Max/MSP/Jitter programmer Kit Clayton, alien FM, computer-music support acts, and a local SuperCollider talk-performance with no pitch deck in sight.

events.title: Unseen Visions: Saturday Daytime Symposium
events.why: A bona fide Bay Area weird-knowledge convening: SF New Age radio, archival films, Continuum, ambient pioneers, and Erik Davis on history and high weirdness—closer to a countercultural field study than nostalgia night.
